title: Axion – Mobile-Driven Desktop Automation
summary: A three-part automation system that lets a user drive and automate their desktop from their phone: a mobile-first Next.js web app, a cloud relay, and a Python desktop agent, with live step-by-step visibility and mid-run steering.
overview: Axion lets someone control and automate their desktop from their phone. It is built from three pieces: a mobile-first Next.js web application, a cloud relay, and a Python desktop application.
The user types a prompt or speaks into the web app; that becomes a task which travels through the relay to the desktop agent, which carries it out.
problem: Desktop automation normally has to be set up and watched at the desktop itself, which is exactly where the user is not when they want it to run.
solution: Split the system so intent is captured on the phone, transport is handled by a cloud relay, and execution stays on the desktop — with each step streamed back so the user can follow along and intervene.

howItWorks.title: Task creation on mobile
howItWorks.description: The user types a prompt or uses voice input in the mobile-first web application, which creates a task.

howItWorks.title: Cloud relay
howItWorks.description: The task is pushed to a cloud relay that sits between the phone and the desktop.

howItWorks.title: Desktop execution
howItWorks.description: The Python desktop application picks the task up from the relay and executes it on the machine.

howItWorks.title: Watch and steer
howItWorks.description: Every step of the run is visible from the phone, and the user can steer the task midway instead of only seeing the final result.

buildingProcess.title: Mobile-first web application
buildingProcess.description: Built the Next.js web application around prompt and voice entry on a phone, and around following a run in progress.

buildingProcess.title: Cloud relay
buildingProcess.description: Built the relay that carries tasks from the web application to the desktop agent.

buildingProcess.title: Python desktop agent
buildingProcess.description: Built the desktop application that receives tasks and automates actions on the machine.

challenges.challenge: An automated run that the user cannot see or correct is difficult to trust.
challenges.solution: Streamed each step back to the phone and allowed the user to steer the task while it is still running.
challenges.lesson: Visibility and the ability to intervene matter as much as the automation itself.

features: Prompt and voice task entry from a mobile-first web app
Cloud relay between phone and desktop
Python desktop agent that executes tasks
Step-by-step visibility of a running task
highlights: Built a three-part system — mobile-first Next.js web app, cloud relay, and Python desktop agent — for driving desktop automation from a phone.
Turned prompt or voice input into tasks that are relayed to the desktop and executed there.
Streamed every step of a run back to the phone and allowed the user to steer the task midway.
lessonsLearned: How to design a system that spans a phone, a relay, and a desktop agent without any of them being able to assume the others are reachable.
That keeping a human able to intervene mid-run is a design requirement for automation, not an extra.
